about: Harder end-to-end evaluation questions (ids 101+): plain-language, Hinglish, two-Act, BNS-versus-IPC and questions that must come back 'not found'. DRAFT: the expected sections were written by Claude and are NOT yet checked by a lawyer. Each gold has `act` (title prefix in Neon), `section` (for humans) and `anchor` (text that must appear in the section body, used to find it in Neon). `expect: notfound` means the right answer is that the sources do not contain it. `oldLaw` is the repealed section number the answer should mention as 'previously ...' (rule: answer from the current law, name the old one). `review` is the note for the lawyer.

questions.question: My tenant isn't paying rent, what can I do?

golds.anchor: by forfeiture

questions.review: Central law only gives notice/forfeiture (TPA s.106, 111(g)); eviction for non-payment is mostly State rent-control law. Is s.111 the right anchor? s.106 and s.108 are mangled in the data (contents-list text), so only s.111 can be scored.

questions.question: A car hit my father and drove away. How do we claim compensation?

golds.anchor: hit and run motor accident

questions.review: s.161 (hit and run compensation scheme); s.166 (application for compensation) also relevant.

questions.question: Can the police arrest me without a warrant?

golds.anchor: when police may arrest without warrant

questions.review: BNSS s.35 (CrPC s.41). Also s.35(3) notice of appearance for offences up to 7 years.

questions.question: I lent my friend money three years ago. Is it too late to file a case to get it back?

golds.anchor: for money payable for money lent

questions.review: Art. 19 of the Schedule: three years from when the loan is made (Art. 21 if payable on demand). Section 3 and 5 also relevant. Data note: Limitation Act has only 43 sections in the data.

questions.question: I think I may be arrested in a false case. Can I get bail before they arrest me?

golds.anchor: reason to believe that he may be arrested on an accusation of having committed a non bailable offence

questions.review: Anticipatory bail, BNSS s.482 (CrPC s.438).

questions.question: My husband beats me. What law protects me?

golds.act: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
golds.anchor: protection orders
subjects such woman to cruelty

questions.review: PWDVA s.18 protection orders (also s.3 definition, s.12 application) and BNS s.85 (cruelty by husband or relatives; IPC 498A).

questions.question: What is the punishment for drunk driving?

golds.anchor: driving by a drunken person

questions.review: MV Act s.185.

questions.question: Can I file for divorce in the first year of marriage?

golds.anchor: no petition for divorce to be presented within one year of marriage

questions.review: HMA s.14 (one-year bar, with leave for exceptional hardship). Applies to Hindus; other communities have their own Acts.

questions.question: cheque bounce ho gaya kya karu

golds.anchor: receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid

questions.review: NI Act s.138: written demand notice within 30 days of the bank's return memo, 15 days to pay, then complaint within one month (s.142).

questions.question: police meri FIR darj nahi kar rahi, ab kya karu

golds.anchor: information in cognizable cases

questions.review: BNSS s.173 (CrPC s.154): send to the Superintendent of Police (s.173(4)), then Magistrate (s.175(3)).

questions.question: kisi ne mera phone chura liya, uski saza kya hai

golds.anchor: whoever commits theft shall be punished

questions.review: BNS s.303(2) theft. Snatching is s.304 - check which the lawyer prefers for a stolen phone.

questions.question: dahej ke liye sasural wale pareshan kar rahe hain, kaunsi dhara lagegi

golds.anchor: subjects such woman to cruelty
penalty for giving or taking dowry

questions.review: BNS s.85-86 (cruelty incl. dowry demand), Dowry Prohibition Act s.3 and s.4; BNS s.80 only if death.

questions.question: non bailable case mein bail kaise milti hai

golds.anchor: when bail may be taken in case of non bailable offence

questions.review: BNSS s.480 (CrPC s.437).

questions.question: RTI ka jawab nahi aaya to appeal kahan karni hai

golds.anchor: any person who does not receive a decision within the time specified

questions.review: RTI Act s.19(1): first appeal to the officer senior to the PIO within 30 days; second appeal s.19(3) to the Information Commission within 90 days.

questions.question: Someone cheated people online using my password. What is the punishment, and how do I prove the messages in court?

golds.anchor: punishment for cheating by personation by using computer resource
admissibility of electronic records

questions.review: IT Act s.66C/66D and BSA s.63 (certificate for electronic records; IEA s.65B before). IT Act s.66 and s.43 are missing in the data.

questions.question: A company's director signed a cheque that bounced. Is the director personally liable, and can it also be cheating?

golds.anchor: offences by companies
whoever by deceiving any person fraudulently or dishonestly induces

questions.review: NI Act s.141 (vicarious liability, in charge and responsible) and BNS s.318 (cheating, IPC 420) - cheating needs dishonest intention at the start.

questions.question: Is a contract signed by a 16 year old valid, and can a child be punished for a crime?

golds.anchor: who are competent to contract
act of a child under seven years of age

questions.review: Contract Act s.11 (minor's agreement void), BNS s.20 (under 7) and s.21 (7 to 12 with immature understanding); Juvenile Justice Act 2015 also matters for 16-year-olds, not in this set.

questions.question: My husband is cruel and does not support me. Can he be punished and can I get monthly maintenance?

golds.anchor: subjects such woman to cruelty
order for maintenance of wives children and parents

questions.review: BNS s.85 (IPC 498A) and BNSS s.144 (CrPC s.125).

questions.question: Does the limitation period apply to arbitration, and how long do I have to file a suit for a loan I gave?

golds.anchor: the limitation act 1963 36 of 1963 shall apply to arbitrations
for money payable for money lent

questions.review: Arbitration s.43(1) and Limitation Act Schedule Art. 19 (3 years). Arbitration s.34 is mangled in the data (Schedule text), so not used.

questions.question: What is the punishment for murder under IPC section 302?

golds.anchor: whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life

questions.review: IPC 302 is repealed from 1 July 2024; the current law is BNS s.103(1). Answer should say 'previously IPC s.302'.

questions.question: IPC 420 cheating punishment

golds.anchor: whoever by deceiving any person fraudulently or dishonestly induces

questions.review: BNS s.318(4) (cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property): up to 7 years and fine. Old IPC 420.

questions.question: Is section 498A of the IPC still law?

golds.anchor: subjects such woman to cruelty

questions.review: Replaced by BNS s.85 and s.86 (cruelty defined).

questions.question: What is the new section for criminal conspiracy, earlier 120B?

golds.anchor: when two or more persons agree with the common object to do or cause to be done

questions.review: BNS s.61 (IPC 120A and 120B).

questions.question: What is the punishment for theft under IPC section 379?

golds.anchor: whoever commits theft shall be punished

questions.review: BNS s.303(2): up to 3 years, or fine, or both; community service for first-time theft under Rs 5,000 if the property is returned. Old IPC 379: up to 3 years.
